title: Former fighters protest conditions at the Buea DDR centre
location: Buea, South-West Region; Borstal Institute/Bokwaongo road area
organizer: Former residents of the Buea DDR centre; no formal group identified
threshold_50_evidence: No source reports a demonstration headcount. S009 says 70 ex-combatants were selected “among the strikers” for payments, but does not say they were the road protest attendance.

start_date.summary: MMI and Recorderline date the Buea action to 1 February; Actu Cameroun also places the protest on 1 February.

location.summary: Roadblocks in Buea around Bokwango/Bokwaongo and Borstal Institute junction; spellings vary by source.

organizer.summary: The reports identify former fighters at the Buea DDR centre; no formal group is named.

demands.summary: Reports describe complaints about feeding, living conditions and unfulfilled government job/reintegration promises. No supplied category specifically captures this set of demands.

participants_original.summary: No crowd count. The 70 selected recipients in S009 are not explicitly the road-protest headcount.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Attendance of 50 or more is not established; no numeric gathering count is reported.

end_date.summary: No physical ending time/date is reported.

protester_violence.summary: No adequate affirmative or explicit absence evidence; unknown.

state_response.summary: Officials met with protesters and offered review; Actu Cameroun, citing Mutations, reports payments to selected former fighters. Accommodation is coded yes as reported; implementation and full resolution are not independently verified; other response dimensions remain unknown.

notes: MMI reports roadblocks at Bokwango and passers-by turned away. Recorderline gives a Borstal Institute–Bokwaongo route and says officials met protesters. Actu Cameroun cites Mutations for 70 aid recipients, not attendance. VOA S007 says a Buea protest occurred about a week before the 15 February Bamenda march, while S005/S009/S010 place this reported action on 1 February and MMI S006 says only “days back.” The timing could be imprecise or could refer to a second Buea action; it is unresolved. The staging-domain CrisisWatch search result and retrospective results remain discovery-only and do not resolve the chronology.
open_questions: How many people joined the street protest?
When did the blockade physically end?
Was there a separate Buea DDR protest around 8 February, or is VOA’s relative timing imprecise?
What source lineage links the Mutations account and other Buea reporting?
Were reported payments fully implemented and to whom?

title: Former fighters march from the Bamenda DDR centre to the North-West governor’s office
location: Bamenda, North-West Region; streets to the governor’s office
organizer: Former fighters residing at the Bamenda DDR centre; no formal group named
threshold_50_evidence: No source gives march attendance. VOA’s figure of more than 150 refers to people in dispute at the Bamenda centre, not marchers; its roughly 400 figure covers residents of both Bamenda and Buea centres. The New Humanitarian search result says “dozens,” which is unquantified and below no reliable threshold inference.

start_date.summary: MMI and VOA date the Bamenda street march to Monday 15 February; Cameroon Concord independently reports that date.

location.summary: The reports identify Bamenda and describe movement through streets to the North-West governor’s office.

organizer.summary: Former residents/ex-fighters at the Bamenda DDR centre; no named formal organization.

demands.summary: Reports describe missing allowances, living conditions and unfulfilled government reintegration promises. No supplied category precisely captures the DDR grievances.

participants_original.summary: No march headcount reported. Centre-resident totals are not protest attendance.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: No source establishes 50 or more marchers; the retrospective search-result phrase “dozens” is not a precise count and remains discovery-only.

protester_violence.summary: No adequate affirmative or explicit absence evidence; unknown.

state_response.summary: VOA reports grievances forwarded to authorities; Cameroon Concord reports a governor meeting and a post-protest financial package. Accommodation is coded yes as reported, without treating it as complete grievance resolution; other dimensions remain unknown.

notes: The 150+ Bamenda centre residents and approximately 400 residents across the Bamenda and Buea centres in VOA are not march attendance. The New Humanitarian and PILPG search results are retrospective and do not provide an exact crowd count. Cameroon Concord has politically loaded framing and reports a 17 February package; it does not document turnout or a physical end. MMI/VOA/Cameroon Concord coverage shares facts but the articles do not establish independent sourcing.
open_questions: Were any of the reported funds/services delivered and were the written grievances addressed?
Are the multiple outlet accounts independently sourced?

title: Buea taxi drivers block a road after alleged police abuse of a colleague
organizer: Taxi drivers; no formal group identified
threshold_50_evidence: No source reports the number of drivers present; neither article establishes 50 or more participants.

start_date.summary: The February-dated variant says the road blockade occurred on 8 February 2021; this date is disputed by a near-identical 2020-published story.

location.summary: Both versions identify Buea near Congelcam.

organizer.summary: Both versions describe taxi drivers acting collectively; no named formal organization.

demands.summary: The February-dated version says drivers protested an alleged police slap against a colleague; both versions share the same story sequence.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: No count or clear qualitative evidence that at least 50 were assembled.

end_date.summary: The articles give traffic disruption durations (about 45 versus 30 minutes) but do not establish when the protest itself ended.

protester_violence.summary: No adequate affirmative or explicit absence evidence; unknown.

state_response.summary: The alleged slap is described as the precipitating grievance, not as a state response to the demonstration; event-specific response is unknown.

notes: Preserve this as a candidate only: S001 is dated 9 February 2021 and assigns the action to 8 February; S002 is a near-identical Cameroon News Agency item dated 8 July 2020, with the same alleged police slap near Congelcam and the same traffic sequence but a different duration. Their relationship is explicit in the local source cards, and together they do not establish an independent February occurrence. Preserve the February version’s nominal date without treating the episode as confirmed. Keep separate from the Buea DDR protest.
open_questions: Is there independent contemporaneous evidence of a February 2021 taxi-driver protest?
Was the 2021-dated variant a re-dated copy of the 2020 story?
When did the road blockade physically end?
Was there an event-specific state response beyond the alleged precipitating slap?

title: Dschang traders’ action against municipal practices (date unresolved)
organizer: Local merchants/traders; no formal organization named
threshold_50_evidence: The article describes traders’ action but gives no date-specific crowd count or other evidence of 50 or more participants.

start_date.summary: The page is marked added 2 February 2021, but the article does not establish the action date; a publication/added date is not used as the event start.

location.summary: The action is described in Dschang.

organizer.summary: Merchants/traders are described collectively; no named formal organizer.

demands.summary: The report describes complaints about the mayor’s municipal practices, including market rents/contributions and market conditions.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: No crowd number or qualitative evidence establishing at least 50.

end_date.summary: No protest start or physical end established.

protester_violence.summary: No adequate affirmative or explicit absence evidence; unknown.

state_response.summary: The article mentions a local elected official’s account after the action but does not establish an event-specific state response; unknown.

notes: MenouActuWeb reports a “mouvement d’humeur” by merchants denouncing mayoral practices and is marked added 2 February. The actual action date, attendance and exact governmental demand are not established; it may fall outside February. Municipal taxes/rents are treated as a provisional price/tax-policy category only.
open_questions: What precise policy or remedy did they demand from the mayor/council?
What was the action’s physical form and ending?
